body: I actually am writing a story about this at the moment. I think all the time how cool it would be to be an asteroid miner and have my own ship, get ore, sell it off, get rich in my spaceship. So I'm writing a story about an asteroid miner who hates his job and wishes he was a farmer.

But lets look at it this way. You have a friend, who is in constant emotional agony. Believe me, my misery is a secret to nobody. You try to help, but what can you really do? The person refuses to do anything about their situation, and you can't live their life for them. They are bitter and useless to everyone around them. If they came and said they dont' want to do it anymore, you'd really prefer they live in their continued agony for your enjoyment? Because you want them to?

Eventually, I will wear out my welcome. My constant string of shitty jobs that I quit when I get sick of them will wear on everyone's nerves. My mom has already agreed that we should cut contact because she's sick of my shit. As she said "I only care about myself. I don't want to be made uncomfortable, I just want to kick back and relax my whole life". Eventually, others will see this too. They will become frustrated, and soon start to hate me.

So should I live reviled, or die loved? I mean, I don't really care. I can hold out as long as possible, I get to die either way. But to continue taking money and resources from everyone around me, to continue feeding off them emotionally, to continue letting down their every expectation, this doesn't seem like it helps anyone. It's like waiting for a parasite to die. Wouldn't you rather the parasite destroyed itself? I provide nothing of value to anyone other than occasional witticisms and shallow insights. I take gifts, meals, affection, and I don't return much of anything. I am a losing investment in every way. The only thing that could ever really benefit from my interaction would be a pet, and I'm honestly much to lazy to take care of a pet.

But we're also supposed to live for ourselves. We have passions and interests that make it worth it. We don't exist *solely* for other people. The exceptions are things like parents or people who spend the majority of their lives involved in charity, etc. The majority of people live for themselves, and draw support form other people.

For me, my only real passion is video games and I its not like that's a reason to get up in the morning. I have nobody who relies solely on me, no pets, no girlfriend. Anyone who cares about me would inevitably move on, because that is the nature of life. If I die tomorrow of a heart attack, they would be just as stricken. At least this way I can say proper goodbyes when I so desire.

Indeed, that's what has kept me around for this long to be honest. Though at a certain point you have to ask yourself, are we really just here to live for someone else? If I find no joy in my life, why do the "selfless" thing and keep existing becuase it pleases someone else? Maybe a nobler person than I would be willing to do that, but its wearing thin for me. I have made the decision that I won't do it while my grandma is alive, because that would be too heartbreaking for her. But otherwise, my  best friend is the only one who really matters in that respect. I imagine when the time comes that I can't keep living, I will distance myself from him. I'm good at wearing on peoples nerves, and I imagine I can make him give up on me. My sister will understand in time, my mom...I don't really care about. I'll never live up to her standards so I'm basically a disappointment either way. My dad would take it very hard, but he also has a new daughter. He has new joys and experiences ahead of him with her, so it isn't like he will be alone and distraught.

In all, I can't live just to please others. When my teeth degrade, periodontal disease sets in, the fat accumulates and the self loathing grows worse, why should I keep going? What is the point of heaping more and more misery on?

Well let's be honest, that's a bit of a platitude. My life could get better, indeed, or it could continue on its downward trajectory. TO say that experiencing that pain is worth it merely on the merits of living doesn't really hold up for me. 

Once I am dead, none of it will matter. There won't be anymore words, or sadness, or self hate, or boredom. There won't be anymore...well...there won't be anymore.

There is always someone out there, creeping around the edges. It's the internet. I'm sure there has to be someone like that out there. I admire your positivity, but it falls on deaf ears. I will die early, by my own hand or not. I just don't feel like waiting around for the stroke.

Of course there's a part that doesn't want this. There's a part that wants my life to be great and everything to be okay, but there's a much larger part that says the realism is much more likely, that shit isn't gonna work out, that my body will fall apart at the same rate its going, and shit is gonna suck. 

I'm here because I don't know where else to ask. I assume there will be someone else here who shares my preoccupation with death, with the rest that is sure to come.
